findings.text: The rewritten sentence reads 'the median request landed inside the window, and one of the five did not', but the log it names in the same paragraph (live-census-20261117T2145Z.log: counts requested 5, request_lag_seconds p50 96.674459, p90 and max 917.087791, and a row at request_lag_seconds 197.951593) holds two requests outside 120 s, not one: 197.951593 s and 917.087791 s are both counted in the five samples. The repair replaced the false universal with a false count in the same sentence, so the cumulative evidence record still states a population its own log contradicts; the reading the code now computes (late_requests) would report both, and the paragraph should read 'two of the five' and name the 197.951593 s request beside the 917.1 s one.

The two quantile assertions compare the census's p50 and max against the lags the test itself wrote into the receipts (5 and 917 at line 354), so they move with their own input and stay green under the regression they sit beside: negative-control-dimension-durability.log records that with 6b14ecef07 reverted only the late_requests and request_window_seconds lookups fail, while 371-372 still pass. The guard for the added reading is lines 373-375, and the duplicated quantile expectations restate the earlier case at line 342 rather than protecting the new field.

The only production caller of review_request_census reads census['obligations'] and census['deadline_seconds'] and drops the rest, so late_requests reaches no duty row, log or surface; the fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/dispatch-admission-and-landing-take-seconds/a-delivered-run-is-reviewed-within-minutes.html:113 says the census reports such a run apart, which is true of the returned dict and only readable by a test or a direct caller, not by a coordinator reading the pane.
